transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, the district will administer its required middle-school mathematics assessment on May 14, 2027, and I have the draft administration plan in front of me. Before I give my final approval, I'd like each of you to review the draft and share any concerns or feedback. The plan currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. Please go ahead and take a look, and let me know what you think.

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern with the room arrangement in the draft plan. My finalized roster has 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students to comply with that requirement. However, I should note that this updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker. The draft plan's call for all 26 students testing together in Room 201 would exceed the state limit.

transcript.text: I also have a concern with the draft plan. While reviewing the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment, and they must be four-function calculators — not graphing calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators to be available throughout the entire assessment, which would violate the state manual on both counts: calculator type and timing of use.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical concern with the digital testing component of the draft plan. My device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and the district cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, and they confirmed that paper booklets are authorized as an alternative. However, this result has not yet been added to the plan. The draft plan's call for digital testing on school tablets is not feasible given these findings, and we need to revise the plan to use paper booklets instead.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a concern with the storage provision in the draft plan. My security review of the state testing agreement, which I completed this week, requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan currently calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, which does not meet these requirements. I have not yet updated the storage field in the plan to reflect the correct procedure.

Ensure a second proctor is assigned so that each testing room (Room 201 and Room 202) has its own proctor on the day of assessment.
